'''Dennis A. Dougherty''' (born December 4, 1952, in [[Harrisburg, Pennsylvania|Harrisburg]], [[Pennsylvania]]) is the George Grant Hoag Professor of Chemistry at [[California Institute of Technology]]. His research applies [[physical organic chemistry]] to systems of biological importance.  Dougherty uses various approaches to understand of the human brain, including ''in vivo'' [[Nonsense suppressor|nonsense suppression]], which incorporates [[Non-proteinogenic amino acids|unnatural amino acids]] into [[ion channel]]s for structure-function studies.

==Education==
Dougherty received his B.S. and M.S. in 1974 from [[Bucknell University]]. Subsequently, he earned his Ph.D. in 1978 under the supervision of [[Kurt Mislow]] at [[Princeton University]] and was a post-doctoral scholar in [[Jerome Berson]]'s lab at [[Yale University]] in 1979.

==Career==
In 1979 Dougherty became a member of the Caltech faculty, earning tenure in 1985. He pioneered the investigation of the role of [[cation–π interaction]]s in protein structure, molecular recognition and enzyme catalysis.<ref name="doughertyrev">{{cite journal|last=Dougherty|first=D. A.|author2=J.C. Ma|title=The Cation–π Interaction|journal=Chemical Reviews|year=1997|volume=97|issue=5|pages=1303–1324|doi=10.1021/cr9603744|pmid=11851453}}</ref> He is the scientific co-founder of Neurion Pharmaceuticals, Inc. In 2005 he published a textbook entitled ''Modern Physical Organic Chemistry'' with co-author [[Eric V. Anslyn]]. 

Dougherty is the recipient of multiple teaching awards including the Richard Badger Teaching Award (1992), the ASCIT Excellence in Teaching Award (1987 and 2000), and the Richard P. Feynman Prize for Excellence in Teaching (2010).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.caltech.edu/today|title=Caltech Today - Caltech|website=The California Institute of Technology|accessdate=10 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://provost.caltech.edu/FeynmanTeachingPrize/|title=Richard P. Feynman Prize for Excellence in Teaching - Caltech Office of the Provost|website=Provost.caltech.edu|accessdate=10 August 2017}}</ref>  In 2009, he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www8.nationalacademies.org/onpinews/newsitem.aspx?RecordID=04282009|title=72 New Members Chosen By Academy|website=8.nationa.lacademies.org|accessdate=10 August 2017}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He currently lives in South Pasadena with his wife Dr. Ellen Dougherty, the superintendent of the [[Lawndale Elementary School District]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lawndale Elementary School District|url=http://www.lawndale.k12.ca.us/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=55706&type=d&rn=8044283|url-status=dead|accessdate=2010-06-19|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090831052737/http://www.lawndale.k12.ca.us/apps/pages/index.jsp?uREC_ID=55706&type=d&rn=8044283|archivedate=2009-08-31}}</ref>
